A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–I. Content can be reliably matched across the appendix page shifts.

before.justification: v2 reports original surface and texture reconstruction experiments, runtime measurements, generalization tests and noise-robustness results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and their quantitative and qualitative outcomes, including Tables 1–6 and the appendix reconstructions.

M1.justification: The Matérn reconstruction procedure, Nyström/FALKON variant, texture extension and NKF-based learned kernels are unchanged. The revised neural-network discussion concerns their theoretical characterization.

E1.justification: Both versions use ShapeNet, SRB, GSO and Objaverse with the same reconstruction, texture, out-of-category generalization and noisy-input scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in each matched experiment, including NS/NS* and the kernel-free methods on SRB, arc-cosine for texture, and NKF* and NKSR in the robustness comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices F–H retain the same splits, sample counts, bandwidth sweeps, noise levels, metrics, solvers and timing procedures. Settings appearing on different appendix pages were already documented in v2.

E4.justification: The bandwidth-sensitivity analysis, stationarity examples in Appendix A, noise tests in Table 5, convergence comparison and supplementary qualitative examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version introduces repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates for the reported comparisons.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6, plotted results and qualitative reconstructions retain the same outcomes. For example, Table 4 reports Matérn 1/2 versus NKSR IoU values of 95.3 versus 95.6 in both versions.

T1.justification: Corollary 5 and Appendix E substantially revise the claimed theoretical relationship. v2 asserts RKHS equality between Laplace and first-order arc-cosine kernels and an affine relationship. v3 instead identifies the RKHS with a sum involving zeroth- and first-order arc-cosine terms, explicitly decomposes the fully trained ReLU NTK, and derives scaling plus a positive-definite residual kernel in Equations (14)–(16). Theorem 3 and its existing initialization assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction qualifies the NTK equivalences with fixed bottom-layer weights and, for SIRENs, particular initializations. It also replaces the affine-equivalence claim with scaling plus another kernel. The broad reconstruction and performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds an interpretation of the revised Laplace/arc-cosine relationship through a valid residual kernel and distinguishes the NTK with all parameters trained. Empirical interpretations and existing noise-related qualifications are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times and code/data access information are retained. The ShapeNet, SRB and texture details shift across appendix pages without new technical disclosures.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work section are unchanged, but the relationship to prior arc-cosine/ReLU-NTK results is qualified. Appendix E now invokes the already cited Chen and Xu (2021) for the full NTK decomposition instead of directly identifying it with the first-order arc-cosine kernel.

P1.justification: Rewriting is localized to introductory qualifications, Corollary 5 and its proof, with an additional explanatory paragraph. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures and tables retain their content and display structure. The expanded proof changes equation layout and reflows subsequent appendix text; for example, Section H.1 begins on page 21 instead of page 19.

improvement.justification: v3 improves theoretical precision by distinguishing fixed-layer and fully trained NTKs and replacing v2's direct equivalence claim with an explicit decomposition and residual-kernel derivation in Corollary 5 and Appendix E. The introductory qualifications also better reflect the existing theorem assumptions. This is a focused improvement to the argument; the reconstruction method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
